newsitem.title: RUSSIA: AGROKHLEB-Russia wheat, flour imports to stay high.
newsitem.headline: AGROKHLEB-Russia wheat, flour imports to stay high.

text.p: The following is a direct contribution from SovEcon Ltd, an independent research organisation specialising in agricultural production and trade in the former Soviet Union.
RUSSIAN WHEAT IMPORTS CONTINUE TO INCREASE
MOSCOW, June 4 - SovEcon's estimate for Russia's total wheat imports (including wheat flour in grain equivalent) over 1996/97 is now 2.2 million tonnes.
Tight wheat stocks in most wheat surplus areas have resulted in seriously reduced domestic milling wheat offers this spring.
In March-April, wheat was offered mainly from Western Siberia.
However, with the start of a Russian-Uzbek milling-wheat-for-cotton barter deal, tradeable wheat stocks in Western Siberia have also declined.
Negligible domestic milling offers have enforced Russian wheat-consuming provinces to continue importing wheat.
In April, total wheat imports soared nearly two times on the previous month's level. Wheat flour imports rose as well.
Kazakhstan still accounts for the bulk of Russia's wheat imports. The country has also increased its flour exports to Russia and has emerged as Russia's leading wheat flour supplier.
Despite financial constraints limiting effective demand, the Russian wheat consuming provinces, particularly in the European part of Russia, have to increase their wheat imports.
It is likely that imports will remain at a high level until the beginning of the 1997 harvest.
